designSummary: Stepped design with four hospitals and six three-month periods (one baseline period in all hospitals, then one hospital introduced every three months in a random order), restricted to adult ward calls; linear mixed model for time to first critical intervention with period and phase as fixed effects.
sampleSize: About 2,310 adult ward calls a year give about 145 calls per hospital per three-month period, or about 3,470 calls over 18 months. With a standard deviation of 6 minutes and an intracluster correlation of 0.04 (claim c4), the stepped design with four hospitals and six periods has roughly 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 to detect a 2-minute reduction, which is smaller than the 3.1-minute fall seen in the five-hospital evaluation. Because four clusters give few degrees of freedom, the analysis uses a small-sample correction and the result is reported as an estimate with its interval, not a verdict. Unplanned intensive care admission (intracluster correlation 0.02, about 12 percent of calls) is underpowered for an effect of the size seen elsewhere and is reported descriptively with its interval.
primaryAnalysis: Linear mixed model for log-transformed time to first critical intervention with fixed effects for period (calendar time) and programme phase, a random effect for hospital and a hospital-by-period random effect, Kenward-Roger small-sample correction; the phase effect is back-transformed to a ratio of median times with its 95 percent confidence interval.
secondaryAnalysis: Logistic mixed model for unplanned intensive care admission within 12 hours with the same structure; descriptive counts of deaths within 24 hours by phase; run charts of simulations delivered and latent safety threats resolved; framework analysis of interviews and debrief observations, integrated with the quantitative results in a joint display by hospital.
missingData: Calls with a missing first-intervention time are counted by hospital and phase; if more than 5 percent are missing, multiple imputation by chained equations with 20 imputations under a missing-at-random assumption, with a complete-case sensitivity analysis.
multiplicity: One primary outcome; secondary and balancing outcomes are reported with intervals and are not tested for significance.
software: R with lme4 and pbkrtest for the quantitative strand; NVivo for the qualitative strand.
overfittingGuards: Model structure and adjustment variables fixed before data collection
No subgroup analysis by hospital beyond the joint display
Checklist scores from simulations kept as a secondary description (claim c2)
summary: About 145 adult ward calls per hospital per period give roughly 80 percent power for a 2-minute reduction with a small-sample correction.
